September 20, 2026

State Department issues Middle East travel advisory as Trump cuts Camp David trip short

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The State Department issued a broad travel advisory for the Middle East, warning that the security environment remains complex with potential for unforeseen escalation, flight cancellations and airspace closures, and advising Americans to reconsider travel to and through the region. US embassies across the Middle East issued parallel security alerts, and President Trump returned to the White House early from Camp David, with aides citing the potential for major escalation. Iran issued a Code 100 alert, its highest-level national security alert, placing the IRGC and other national security bodies on notice. No specific military action had been confirmed at the time of the warnings.

Ukraine launches its largest drone assault on Russia, striking Moscow

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Ukraine launched more than 1,600 drones at strategic sites across Russia, including hundreds directed at Moscow itself, in what is described as its largest attack of the war. Reports indicate Ukraine also used its Flamingo cruise missile in the strikes. The assault came on the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections and follows days of European warnings about Russian activity.

US military finds faulty AI and intelligence caused strike on Iranian school

tags: war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

A US military investigation determined that faulty AI, intelligence and satellite imagery led to a February 28 missile strike on an all-girls school in Iran. Two Tomahawk missiles hit the school, and reporting places the death toll at more than 150 people, including at least 123 children. Pentagon personnel knew within hours that the United States was responsible, and the probe described a cascade of preventable failures. The president has continued to deny US responsibility for the strike, contradicting his own defence and intelligence agencies.

Hegseth uses scripture to address troops on Pentagon 'Send Me' tour

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth opened a military tour in Texas by quoting Isaiah 6:8, telling service members that across 250 years Americans had raised their hands and said 'send me' — to fight the redcoats, the communists and the Islamists. The remarks were posted by the Department of Defense rapid response account. The tour coincided with a promotional video posted by President Trump framing his presidency in terms of destiny and divine deliverance and citing strikes on Iran's nuclear sites and a Maduro operation alongside recruitment figures. Critics say the language echoes holy war rhetoric and invokes religion to justify military deployment.

UnitedHealth accused in lawsuit of using AI tool with 90% error rate to deny care

tags: health, legal, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

A class action pending in Minnesota alleges UnitedHealth used an algorithm called NH Predict to set coverage limits for Medicare Advantage patients in post-acute care, overriding physicians' judgments with rigid recovery predictions. The complaint says the model has a 90% error rate and that the company relied on it knowing few patients appeal; a KFF analysis found only 0.2% of denied claims are appealed. Named cases include a 91-year-old man whose family paid $150,000 after coverage ended at 19 days, and a stroke patient whose family paid roughly $70,000 after denials at 20 and 40 days. A judge has ordered UnitedHealth to open its records in the case.

BLM reviewing 12 data centers on 17,600 acres of public land without public notice

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Bureau of Land Management is reviewing at least 12 data center proposals covering roughly 17,600 acres of public land across six Western states. The largest, about 10,200 acres near Green River, Utah, would pair a nuclear plant with a data center; it was not listed on BLM's website and officials in five of the six states were unaware of the proposals. A reporter located the Utah site in right-of-way records, and within hours the company said it was no longer pursuing it. Eleven proposals remain under review in Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon and Wyoming, classed as 'early stage' and therefore without a public comment period; polling cited puts opposition to local data centers at 70%, with more than 500 towns and counties restricting or banning them this year.

Trump says Washington arch will be built as a military installation

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

President Trump said the triumphal arch he plans to build in Washington, DC will be designated a top-grade military complex capable of housing snipers, sniper ammunition and drones on its roof. The designation follows the same national security rationale used to secure Supreme Court approval for his ballroom project, which critics say is a route around construction regulations and other approval requirements.

Trump privately concedes his own policies are driving expected midterm losses

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

According to the Washington Post, President Trump has acknowledged privately for the first time that Republican losses expected in November stem in part from his own policies. Advisers have become increasingly blunt in telling him that polling is rough and projections are bleak. Factors cited include record high gas and diesel prices and an ongoing war. Publicly the president has continued to express confidence about the midterms.

Netanyahu pushes bills to strip citizenship over criticism of IDF soldiers

tags: politics, media, legal
sources: @groundnews

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he will advance two bills: one to revoke the citizenship of people who slander IDF soldiers, and another to multiply available defamation damages twentyfold. He announced the measures after the documentary 'NAZA' won a prize at the Venice Film Festival. The film uses anonymous testimony from Israeli soldiers and intelligence officials and accuses the military of conduct that could constitute war crimes. Netanyahu called on all Knesset factions that support Zionism to back both bills.

Officials say Pentagon database undercounts US military deaths in the Middle East

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon's public database lists 18 US military deaths. Officials familiar with internal data say the actual Middle East count is at least 22.

Family sues Texas attorney general over abortion denied to dying pregnant woman

tags: legal, health, politics
sources: @groundnews

The family of Tierra Walker, a 37-year-old Texas woman who died in 2024 at 20 weeks pregnant from hypertensive cardiovascular disease and preeclampsia, has sued state officials and medical providers. The lawsuit says Walker requested an abortion as her health deteriorated but doctors did not offer one, and that two physicians had documented a high risk of death before her final hospitalization. Texas law bans most abortions but permits them when a pregnancy threatens the patient's life. The suit names Attorney General Ken Paxton, medical officials and doctors, alleging the ban created fear around providing care.

Trump confirms son received Russian oligarch's funding for wedding celebrations

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

President Trump said Donald Trump Jr. repaid Russian businessman Umar Kremlev after Kremlev funded parts of his wedding celebrations. ProPublica reported the gift was worth hundreds of thousands of dollars and covered events including a private island in the Bahamas and a fireworks show. Kremlev leads the International Boxing Association, an ally of Vladimir Putin, and the organisation has received financing from Russia's state-owned Gazprom. Trump Jr. and his wife Bettina Anderson described the funding as a generous wedding gift from a friend.

Education Department post follows Texas candidate's racist message about UT students

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education posted an image of the University of Texas stadium captioned 'make college football great again' within hours of a post by Bo French, a Republican nominee for statewide office in Texas, that criticised University of Texas students for not being white. French's post drew rebuke from Republicans but remains online, and the White House has not distanced itself from it.

Federal prosecutors charge three with stealing $12 million in Los Angeles homelessness aid

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles charged three nonprofit officials with stealing about $12 million in homelessness aid, alleging the funds went to real estate, luxury travel, vintage vehicles and personal expenses. Prosecutors said Michael Young misused about $7.5 million through shell companies, Donye Mitchell diverted grant money and remains a fugitive, and Lakiya Malone accepted more than $180,000 in bribes. A fourth nonprofit executive, Alexander Soofer, pleaded guilty to stealing at least $2 million. The case follows charges against 12 people accused of stealing more than $10 million in childcare aid, and comes as audits have found oversight gaps in the roughly $1 billion Los Angeles spends annually on homelessness.

Virginia declares drought emergency after hay yields fall 35%

tags: climate, markets
sources: @groundnews

Governor Abigail Spanberger declared a 45-day state of emergency after drought cut statewide hay yields by 35%, creating a 500,000-ton shortage. The order eases transportation rules for larger hay loads to reduce delivery costs. Cattle and calves are Virginia's second-largest agricultural commodity at about $712 million in 2024, with milk fourth at $363 million, and higher feed costs could push up beef and dairy prices regionally. Virginia Tech says producers are weighing early culling and weaning against supplemental feed costs as winter reserves are drawn down early.

Boebert faces sworn ethics complaint alleging relationships with three staffers

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A sworn ethics complaint filed with the US House Committee on Ethics alleges Representative Lauren Boebert had sexual relationships with three House employees under her direct supervision, in violation of a post-MeToo House rule barring members from relationships with their own staff. The complaint, filed under penalty of perjury by David Wheeler of American Muckrakers and first reported by the Colorado Times Recorder, names three current and former senior aides and asserts Boebert arranged a $200,000 payment to one of them, former Colorado state representative Clarice Navarro, to prevent a separate ethics complaint. Navarro called the allegations entirely false, defamatory and without any truth. The allegations are untested.

Viral World War III claims debunked amid genuine Middle East alerts

tags: media, war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Amid 'World War III' trending across social platforms, several widely shared claims were addressed: the United States did not strike Iran overnight, there was no known US military activity over the Middle East, no US strike on Yemen was ordered, and no draft is planned. Houthi forces did strike Saudi Arabia the previous day as part of an ongoing regional exchange, and North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles overnight consistent with its repeated tests. European countries have for months been preparing for a possible Russian provocation against NATO. Confirmed developments include Middle East travel warnings and embassy alerts, Trump's early return from Camp David, and Netanyahu cancelling parts of his US trip to attend only the UN General Assembly.
